expected_outcome: The open gripper moves toward the right cabinet and faces its drawer front.
subgoal: Move toward the right drawer and turn the gripper toward its front.
summary: All three views place the target drawer to the robot's right below the countertop. The arm uses base-frame deltas with 0.05 m translation and 0.5 rad rotation scales; I will move right and lower while rotating away from the downward pose.

expected_outcome: The wrist lowers toward drawer height and moves farther right, with the fingers increasingly forward-facing.
subgoal: Continue positioning above the right drawer.
summary: The gripper moved right only about 8 cm and remains well above the handle. I will continue the same free-space motion; the measured response is smaller than the nominal delta scale.

expected_outcome: The gripper centers nearer the handle, and the wrist view points toward the drawer face.
subgoal: Align the gripper with the right drawer handle.
summary: The right camera shows the open gripper left of the handle and slightly high; the wrist camera shows it tilted upward. I will shift farther right, lower it, and correct the pitch before approaching.

expected_outcome: The gripper clears the edge, lowers, and turns toward a level approach.
subgoal: Clear the counter edge and lower to handle height.
summary: The wrist view still looks upward, and one finger is less open than the other despite an open command, suggesting contact. I will withdraw and lower while correcting pitch in free space.

expected_outcome: The handle moves toward the wrist-view center and the jaws align above and below its bar.
subgoal: Center on the handle and orient the fingers to pinch its horizontal bar.
summary: The wrist camera now clearly sees the drawer face, with the handle right of center. The gripper is below the handle in the external view; I will shift right and slightly up while rolling the fingers for a vertical pinch.

expected_outcome: The drawer handle appears straighter and larger as the gripper approaches its front.
subgoal: Square the gripper to the drawer and approach.
summary: The handle is visible but oblique in the wrist view, and proprioception shows the fingers point partly left and up. I will correct that orientation and advance a short distance while keeping the jaws open.

expected_outcome: The handle moves toward the center between the open fingers and grows in the wrist view.
subgoal: Bring the open jaws toward the handle center.
summary: The bar is nearly vertical in the rolled wrist view, consistent with jaws pinching across its thickness. It remains to the right of the view center, which now corresponds mainly to downward motion; I will lower slightly and advance.

expected_outcome: The bar shifts left toward the center of the wrist image if the vertical alignment correction is appropriate.
summary: The handle is larger but still offset to the right in the wrist view. I will make a small downward adjustment without advancing to verify the image response before grasping.

expected_outcome: The bar enters the space between the fingers without pushing the drawer face.
subgoal: Position the jaws around the handle.
summary: The handle shifted left as expected and is now close to centered across the jaw opening. I will lower a little more and advance slowly; depth remains uncertain from the images.

expected_outcome: The fingertips straddle the handle bar at grasping depth.
subgoal: Complete the slow approach to the bar.
summary: The bar is centered near the finger gap, but the external view still suggests the gripper is in front of it. I will advance another small increment with the jaws open.

expected_outcome: The fingers close against the bar rather than fully together.
subgoal: Close the fingers on the handle.
summary: The handle fills the wrist view and forward travel has slowed, suggesting the fingers are near the drawer. I will close in place to test whether the bar is captured.

expected_outcome: The drawer front follows the gripper outward if the handle is secured.
subgoal: Test the grasp with a short outward pull.
summary: The fingers stopped partly closed around the handle area, which is consistent with contact but does not yet prove a secure grasp. I will pull straight back briefly and check for drawer motion.

expected_outcome: A clear gap and drawer interior become visible above the moving drawer front.
summary: The wrist moved back about 4 cm while the handle retained nearly the same apparent size and position, and the drawer front shifted outward in the external view. This supports a secured grasp, so I will continue pulling.

expected_outcome: The drawer extends farther and exposes more of its interior.
summary: Both external views show the right drawer protruding from the cabinet, while the handle remains held steadily in the wrist view. I will continue the outward pull to make the opening unambiguous.

expected_outcome: The fingers release the bar while the drawer stays open.
summary: The right drawer now projects substantially from the cabinet, after roughly 31 cm of outward wrist motion with a stable handle grasp. I will open the fingers in place and verify that the drawer remains extended.
